text: <s>[INST] How should an investor interpret rising days sales outstanding (DSO)? [/INST] Rising DSO — the average number of days a company takes to collect payment after a sale — is a warning signal. It can indicate: (1) customers are under financial stress and paying more slowly; (2) the company is extending looser credit terms to inflate revenue recognition; (3) revenue may be overstated if receivables are growing faster than sales. Sustained DSO increases, especially when diverging from industry peers, warrant scrutiny of revenue quality and working capital management.</s>

<s>[INST] What does negative free cash flow indicate? [/INST] Negative free cash flow means the company is spending more cash than it generates from operations, after capital expenditures. This can be intentional during high-growth phases where companies reinvest heavily, or a warning sign if persistent without a clear growth thesis. Context is critical: Amazon ran negative FCF for years while building infrastructure.</s>
